text:
If you’re heading onto the waterfront, take the lake wind advisory seriously today: south winds build from 10 knots or less to 15 to 25 knots, with 1- to 2-foot waves. Burlington starts crisp and clear at 45, then turns into a mostly sunny, seasonable day with a high right around 70. Clouds thicken this afternoon, and the south wind will make the lake feel rougher than town. Tonight brings a slight shower chance between 2 and 5, with winds gusting 30 to 35 knots over the broad water and waves building as high as 4 feet.

Wednesday looks warmer, mostly cloudy, and near 77, but the forecast confidence is softer than that number suggests. The European and Canadian-side guidance is notably wetter than the official call, so I’d keep a rain jacket nearby even though the forecasters still lean primarily dry. The lake should stay choppy early Wednesday before easing. Good day for land-based plans today, but I’d finish any boating well before tonight’s gusts arrive.
